summary: Recent updates to the WebRender bindings in Firefox have focused on improving graphics performance and memory management during web page rendering. One key change is the ability to **use EGL (a platform interface for rendering APIs) for creating the rendering context** on macOS, which may lead to smoother graphics and better integration with specific hardware. Additionally, there have been enhancements in managing memory, particularly by fixing leaks in helper classes and ensuring that worker threads clean up properly during shutdown. These improvements not only contribute to a more stable browser experience by reducing crashes and performance hitches but also support new technologies like HDR video through better shader usage, making visual content richer for users.
